meetings.headline: Commission heard the town's request to demolish 30 School Street, then set a vote for March 21.

what_happened.line: The commission closed the public hearing on the town's application to alter or demolish 30 School Street without voting on it.
A special meeting to vote on the certificate was set for Monday the 21st at 7:30, and the applicant agreed to the timeline.
A written decision is to go to the town manager the day after the vote.
Most speakers favored demolition, citing safety, property value and a lack of any viable use; one opposed, calling the building sound.
The hearing turned heated over the commission's handling of the process and a select board letter read into the record.

why_it_matters: The commission's vote decides whether the town may demolish a vacant town-owned building, and the costs raised in the hearing (renovation, upkeep, police and facilities time) are paid from the town budget, mostly taxes.
The cost of renovating or preserving the building was asserted by speakers, not shown in documents at the hearing, and town meeting has not approved paying for renovation or a sale.
